(a) In General.—Subparagraph (C) of section 199(d)(8) is amended—
        (1) by striking “first 6 taxable years” and inserting “first 8 taxable years”, and 
        (2) by striking “January 1, 2012” and inserting “January 1, 2014”.  
    (b) Effective Date.—The amendments made by this section shall apply to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2011.

fable.w: This section only extends a tax provision by changing the number of taxable years and a date, and sets an effective date. There is no tempting participation reading: no outside party is consulted, no hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue is created.
fable.s: by striking “first 6 taxable years” and inserting “first 8 taxable years”

qwen_block.w: This section merely amends specific dates and time periods within an existing tax statute. It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties. The text is purely technical and legislative, containing no mechanism for external participation in a federal decision.
qwen_block.s: (a) In General.—Subparagraph (C) of section 199(d)(8) is amended— (1) by striking “first 6 taxable years” and inserting “first 8 taxable years”, and (2) by striking “January 1, 2012” and inserting “January 1, 2014”. (b) Effective Date.—The amendments made by this section shall apply to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2011.

opus.w: The section only changes a tax provision by extending a period from 6 to 8 taxable years and moving a date from 2012 to 2014. Nothing requires the federal government to consult or coordinate with outside parties before deciding anything. It does not provide for rulemaking, a comment period, a hearing, an advisory body, or a right to sue, so nothing in it could plausibly count as participation.
opus.s: by striking “first 6 taxable years” and inserting “first 8 taxable years”

qwen_chat.w: This section amends specific dates and time periods in the tax code (changing 'first 6 taxable years' to 'first 8 taxable years' and 'January 1, 2012' to 'January 1, 2014'). It does not establish any process for public comment, consultation with outside entities, or advisory committees. The changes are made directly by statute without requiring any participatory mechanism.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that changing tax code provisions affects the public, but the text itself contains no mechanism for public input, consultation, or participation. It is purely a legislative amendment to statutory dates and numbers.
